_meta: A batch of tasks queued at once with different service times, used to show head-of-line (HOL) blocking: a single strict first-in-first-out lane makes one slow task at the head delay every task behind it, even though those tasks are unrelated and quick, and even though no extra work is being done. All tasks are present at time zero; one server processes them one at a time to completion in the chosen order. Under FIFO the tasks are served in arrival order, so if a long task sits at the head, every short task behind it must wait for the long one to finish before it even starts -- its completion time is dominated by work that has nothing to do with it. This is head-of-line blocking: the item at the head of the line holds up the whole line. Reordering the SAME tasks on the SAME single server so the short ones are not trapped behind the long one (here, serving shortest first) leaves the total work and the throughput identical -- the server is busy the whole time either way -- but collapses the mean completion time, because the many short tasks no longer inherit the long task's duration. The lesson is that HOL blocking is an ORDERING effect, not a capacity problem: a strict single FIFO lane couples the latency of unrelated tasks, and the fix is to not force them through one head-blocked lane. service_times lists each task's processing time, in the order they sit in the FIFO queue. It is the fixture; the per-task completion times and mean completion under FIFO order vs shortest-first order, and the identical total work, are computed.
